reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) confirms that W-based HEAs are relevant for plasma-facing applications and can be produced by laser cladding, but none of the passages mention directional solidification, nanolamellar microstructures, or their effects on thermal conductivity or mechanical integrity. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Directional solidification during laser cladding can produce an aligned nanolamellar microstructure in a W-based HEA.
An aligned nanolamellar microstructure creates continuous high-conductivity pathways that markedly improve thermal conductivity.
Coherent interfaces and fine grain structures in such a microstructure preserve mechanical strength and toughness.
The improved thermal conductivity and preserved mechanical properties are maintained under 600–800°C and cyclic loading.
